articles.headline: Filip Forsberg has 2 goals, Juuse Saros gets shutout in Predators' 5th straight win, 3-0 over Kings
keyFacts: Filip Forsberg scored two goals and Juuse Saros made 30 saves as the Nashville Predators defeated the Los Angeles Kings 3-0 on Tuesday night.
The victory extended the Predators winning streak to five games and marked their first shutout of the season for Saros.
The Predators will play at Anaheim on Wednesday night, while the Kings will host the New York Islanders on Thursday night.
body: LOS ANGELES (AP) — Filip Forsberg scored two goals, Juuse Saros made 30 saves in his 28th career shutout and the Nashville Predators extended their winning streak to five games with a 3-0 victory over the Los Angeles Kings on Tuesday night.

Nils Hoglander had two assists and Adam Wilsby got an empty-net goal in the Predators' opener of a five-game West Coast road trip. Saros finished his first shutout of the season with 13 saves in the third period against the Kings' improved effort.
Anton Forsberg stopped 27 shots for the Kings, who were shut out for the first time this season. Los Angeles dropped to 2-3-0 on its seven-game homestand with back-to-back losses .

Nashville scored early in the first period when Hoglander controlled a blue-line turnover by Brian Dumoulin and eventually made a backhand pass through defenseman Cody Ceci's legs to Filip Forsberg for his sixth goal.
Filip Forsberg scored again in the second when Hoglander flipped the puck to him from the boards for an awkward shot that surprised Anton Forsberg.
After a slow offensive start to the season, Filip Forsberg has six goals in his last eight games, including two multigoal games in the past two weeks.
Wilsby's empty-netter, which came on a clearing attempt that took a fortuitous bounce off the boards, was only the third goal of his NHL career and the first since Dec. 20.
Mats Zuccarello returned to Los Angeles' lineup after a six-game injury absence.
Former Kings general manager and defenseman Rob Blake was in attendance. Blake was named the Predators' executive vice president of hockey operations in June.
Up next
Predators: At Anaheim on Wednesday night.
Kings: Host New York Islanders on Thursday night.

articles.headline: Jordan Clarkson toasts Knicks culture after win over Bucks
keyFacts: Jordan Clarkson scored two points in 11 minutes during the New York Knicks 117-85 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks on Tuesday.
Clarkson stated after the game that team culture and staying ready for any amount of playing time are the main focus for the team.
Clarkson is averaging 6.0 points per game this season and is content with his reduced role in contributing to team wins.
body: © Lucas Boland-Imagn Images Jordan Clarkson toasts Knicks culture after win over Bucks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

The transformation Jordan Clarkson has undergone in his career is quite breathtaking. Of course, the physical changes are the most apparent. He changed up his hair and he has both sleeves fully tatted up. But Clarkson has become the quintessential role player, embracing his part to play to help this New York Knicks team achieve their goals.

On Tuesday, Clarkson played just 11 minutes and scored two points on 1-of-5 shooting from the field in a 117-85 win for the Knicks over the Milwaukee Bucks. But his words after the game show that he is all-in on the culture of this team and is willing to do whatever it takes to get his team the victory.

“That’s just our culture here. No matter if it’s one minute, 30 seconds, 30 minutes during the game. That’s what we focus on. That’s what Mike has preached to us since he’s got here and that’s just a big thing all of us hold our hat on,” Clarkson said after the game, via SNY Knicks on X.

"That's just our culture here- no matter if it's one minute, 30 seconds, 30 minutes during the game. That's what we focus on."

— SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) November 11, 2026

Clarkson’s role has been fluctuating over the past year or so, and he’s no longer the Sixth Man of the Year-caliber player he was in years past. Nonetheless, what makes the 34-year-old guard a valuable player for the Knicks despite his decline has been his ability to just stay ready and make the most of his minutes, however many he ends up playing.

Make no mistake about it, Clarkson can still get buckets when called upon. But the Knicks have scarcely needed him to, and yet he’s well content just doing whatever the coaching staff tells him to, which is a testament of the kind of respect the team’s coaching staff commands.

Clarkson is currently averaging just 6.0 points per game, which would be the lowest of his career. But if the Knicks keep on winning games, that should be all that matters to the 34-year-old NBA champion .

articles.headline: Carney on Australia challenge, 'Magic' concept, and 'necessary' domestic limbo
keyFacts: Sky Sports analyst Brian Carney said Australia and New Zealand are deserved finalists for the Rugby League World Cup.
Carney stated that Peter V'Landys and the Australian Rugby League Commission are planning a Magic Weekend style format for the 2030 Rugby League World Cup.
Carney noted that the sport is currently in a domestic limbo as it works toward a potential NRL partnership.
body: Brian Carney on the challenge of usurping Australia, a 'Magic' style 2030 World Cup, and the 'necessary' domestic limbo

Sky Sports Rugby League's Brian Carney takes a look at the upcoming Rugby League World Cup finals, the Rugby League World Cup 2030, and the domestic limbo over the potential NRL partnership on the horizon
Monday 9 November 2026 16:37, UK

Sky Sports Rugby League's Brian Carney analyses the big talking points from the world of rugby league, including the upcoming Rugby League World Cup finals, the 'Magic' style concept for the Rugby League World Cup 2030, and the ongoing work towards an NRL partnership.
The more things change, the more things seem to stay the same.

In a World Cup where we were hailing Tonga and Samoa and their emergence as title contenders, not just for an upset here and there but as title contenders, you have Australia and New Zealand in the final.

Australia and New Zealand are deserved finalists. They opened the tournament with an absolute bell-ringer and we will hope for more of the same in the final.
I really cannot split them. I give New Zealand a really good chance but like Australia have done for nearly half a century now, they keep finding ways to win.
When they are down and out, dead and buried, off their game, like they were against Fiji, they find a way to win.
Kalyn Ponga coming back in for New Zealand was a massive boost and he obviously had no problems defensively off the back of his broken arm- he threw himself into tackles and came up with try-savers.
We are in for a sensational final between the two best nations in the world. There are no complaints there.
In the women's final, I cannot look past the Jillaroos. They are at a level of dominance that I don't think we have ever seen from the Kangaroos ever.
The scorelines they are posting, their ability to win games at a canter, even sometimes leaving points out there.
It is remarkable. It looks a greater hurdle to catch up with them for the likes of New Zealand and Samoa than the hurdle in the men's game.
Will Tonga rue going all out against Samoa?
I do not think there is a huge amount between Australia, New Zealand, Tonga, and Samoa on any given day. I would not have fallen over in shock if Tonga or Samoa had won either of the semi-finals.
I was probably more surprised that Tonga went full-on against Samoa a week earlier in a game that they did not have to win.
They went all out for that game and it would have taken plenty out of both teams heading into the semi-finals.

While I understand and applaud that the emotion of the game and the occasion drove Tonga and Samoa to field strong sides, it didn't make a whole lot of strategic sense for Tonga in particular. They could have rested players and prepared for their semi-final.
That is not what happened.
I was somewhat surprised at that approach not withstanding the fact the game meant so much passion wise.
The whole purpose was to win the World Cup, not to beat Samoa.
Tonga and Samoa's Tier 1 status: A warning shot for England?
In terms of Tonga and Samoa now being given Tier 1 status, I would be surprised if that warning shot wasn't felt all the way back in 2017 when Tonga emerged as a force in international rugby league.
I do not think for a minute that England will have been taken by surprise by the performances of Tonga and Samoa and the subsequent reward which appears to be Tier 1 status.
It is only good for the game and I think people will applaud the efforts that have been made by a variety of people and organisations to get those teams to where they are.
You also have to give a nod to those Tonga players back in 2017. Andrew Fifita, Jason Taumulolo, and Daniel Tupou in particular made the decision to make themselves available to Tonga.
That decision has been the spark that has lit this Pacific rebirth of Tonga and Samoa in international rugby league.
Doing things differently: 'Magic' style in 2030

The Rugby League World Cup 2030 is fascinating. We are told it is going to be a Magic Weekend style event where they will descend upon a city for a weekend, play all the games, then decamp to another host city.
That is not a traditional way of doing a World Cup but the mastermind and the brains behind it is Peter V'Landys and the Australian Rugby League Commission.
The ARLC have all the power, all the money, and at the helm they have a man who, in his professional history, has shown a willingness to challenge the establishment and the status quo.
Cast your minds back to 2017 and the Melbourne Cup, one of the most prestigious horse races in the world.
So, if you are the boss of New South Wales horse racing, how do you try and take on the Melbourne Cup? Do you go like-for-like? No.
V'Landys decided to create something different and did the Everest race. The draw would be done differently; the audience and the sponsors they would be targeting would be very different.
It would look and feel very different to the Melbourne Cup and it has been a roaring success by all metrics.
He is not going to take on, for example, the Rugby Union World Cup and try and go blow for blow with them and replicate what rugby union or football does.
'We are different' is how he thinks and he will think differently and act differently with this Magic style World Cup.
I am fascinated by it. They have got all the wind behind them at the moment. They have all the money and will to do this.
This is the man who brought games to Las Vegas when people said it could and would not happen and it would not be a success.
While it is not for the traditionalists, V'Landys' thinking is what is best for rugby league and he might have landed on something there.
That goes hand-in-hand with the extension of the eligibility rules to great-grandparents because he wants Tonga, Samoa, Fiji, Cook Islands, Papua New Guinea. He wants to secure all of Pacifica.
This is another step towards ensuring that these teams have the players available to them to create stories that resonate back in their countries.
We are a nimble sport because we are small, we have got fewer institutional breaks than others which can be good and bad.
It has allowed the ARLC to determine what international rugby league is going to look like.
When you are paying the piper, you call the tune and the ARLC are paying the piper.
Most people in administrative roles spend their lives trying to solve problems. V'Landys seems to make a living discovering that they weren't problems in the first place.
A necessary domestic limbo?
It is hard to argue that we are not in a case of limbo domestically with so much to be announced and the fact we are in November.
There is a lot going on and if the NRL partnership deal comes to pass, it is a major development in our game and it has taken a long time to get to this point.
If that means a delay on other things, I say so be it. It is not ideal but I won't lose sleep over it.
It might set back planning but if we get where we need to be at the end of it all, I am sure it will be worth it.
Improvement in the domestic game is vital, not just for international rugby league. We need to continuously improve the domestic game for our audiences, who are our most important people.
They are the lifeblood of the sport.
We have to improve it for those people, you have to keep the product on top for those people.

If the domestic game improves, then you would imagine the international game would improve by extension but your focus first and foremost has to be on the fans and ensuring you are giving them a game they want to watch in increasing numbers and are happy with.
That is the only question you need to answer.

articles.headline: College basketball winners, losers: Big early deficits doom No. 3 Illinois in loss at Texas Tech, No. 2 Duke
keyFacts: No. 2 Duke suffered a 79-73 upset loss to No. 5 Michigan State in a marquee Tuesday college basketball matchup.
No. 3 Illinois lost 74-68 to Texas Tech after falling behind by 20 points in the first half.
No. 1 Florida defeated Florida State 81-72 to improve to 2-0 behind Thomas Haugh's double-double.
body: Tuesday's college basketball schedule was heralded as one of the best nonconference days of the season. With close games, upsets and drama in marquee matchups, it's safe to say it lived up to the hype. No. 1 Florida, No. 2 Duke and No. 3 Illinois were all in action against quality opponents away from home. And two of the three went down in defeat.

Florida came away with an 81-72 road win over in-state foe Florida State to move to 2-0, while Duke received a wake-up call with a 79-73 upset loss to No. 5 Michigan State in the Champions Classic. The Fighting Illini weren't so lucky in their road game at No. 16 Texas Tech. The Red Raiders jumped out to a 20-point lead in the first half and held off a rally from Illinois behind 20 points from Cruz Davis in Texas Tech's 74-68 victory.
Not every team playing on Tuesday walked away feeling good after a win.

Michael Malone's North Carolina squad only led by two points at halftime against Wyoming before pulling away in the second half for a 76-63 win. The Tar Heels also received an upset scare in their season-opener against Western Carolina last week before pulling away in the final minutes
After an intense day of hoops, here are the biggest winners and losers from the slate.
Winner: Jeremy Fears Jr. shines vs. Duke

Fears was simply brilliant against Duke. He finished with a double-double (18 points and 11 assists). The way he controls the pace of the game and runs the offense, there are not many players in the sport who do it as well as he does. Fears is the best point guard in America. The way he sets up his teammates for good looks in transition and in half-court sets is unmatched. Fears showed why he was the CBS Sports Preseason POTY. -- Cameron Salerno
Loser: Duke receives a wake-up call

Tuesday should serve as a wake-up call for Duke. Not only did Michigan State beat Duke, but it also dominated from start to finish in the most impressive win by any team in college basketball this season. The Blue Devils couldn't buy a bucket in this game. Part of it was shot selection and the other part was Michigan State's defense, which was so good and physical that Duke couldn't get clean looks.

The bad (maybe, good) news? Duke's schedule gets significantly harder during the next month. Duke faces UConn and Illinois this month. Duke will certainly be tested this season. This game should serve as an early measuring stick for Scheyer's team. -- CS
Loser: Bad vibes for Kentucky already?

Not only did Kentucky look disjointed and overmatched, it also looked timid and disinterested relative to the free-flowing and well-connected Jayhawks. The bench lacked energy, and it was hard not to consider the "what if" factor of Tyran Stokes. Kentucky heavily pursued Kansas' freshman phenom, who is a Louisville native. They lost that recruiting battle and lost out on a great player who brought strong vibes to the matchup. Stokes played with an obvious intensity and joy that was clearly missing from the Kentucky side. This wasn't as bad as bad as Kentucky's 94-59 neutral-site loss to Gonzaga last season. But it should be a wakeup call. Early in a critical third season for coach Mark Pope, UK has a lot to figure out. -- David Cobb
Winner: Texas Tech records huge win over Illinois

You could hear how loud the environment at Texas Tech was by sitting at home with your TV volume on. The atmosphere inside the arena sounded electric. Texas Tech recorded one of the most impressive wins of the season by taking down No. 3 Illinois. A rematch of this game sometime in March would be great when All-Americans on both sides (Illinois' David Mirkovic and Texas Tech's JT Toppin) are cleared to play. Nonetheless, Texas Tech should receive a sizeable boost in next week's AP poll after taking down the No. 3 team in the country. -- CS
Winner: Tyran Stokes has elevated

When the top-rated freshman makes jumpers, Stokes is almost unstoppable. It's early in the cycle, but Stokes looks like a tier above the rest in the early 2027 NBA Draft discourse. The 6-foot-8 bullyball wing was phenomenal, totaling 23 points, 10 rebounds and four assists. Kentucky had absolutely no answer for the big dawg. -- Isaac Trotter
Loser: North Carolina receives a scare from Wyoming

For the second time in three games, it got scary for North Carolina. In Malone's debut at UNC, the Tar Heels were in a close game with Western Carolina before pulling away down the stretch. Against Wyoming, UNC led by only two points at halftime before outscoring the Cowboys by double digits in the second half. With a game against Georgia looming at home later this week, the Tar Heels will have to play better or risk not escaping with a win. -- CS
Winner: Florida picks up win over another in-state rival

Florida played a C+ game against Miami last week and came away with a double-digit win. Tuesday's showdown against in-state foe Florida State was a lot more of a hostile environment than the very pro-Gators crowd Todd Golden's team played in front of during a season opener against Miami in Tampa. FSU made things very interesting in the second half, cutting the deficit to four with less than seven minutes remaining. However, Florida was able to close things out behind another double-double (21 points and 10 rebounds) from star forward Thomas Haugh.
Florida State played teams extremely tough during Year 1 of Luke Loucks' tenure at his alma mater. This game showed the Seminoles will make some real noise in the ACC this season. -- CS
Winner: Vanderbilt makes a statement vs. Memphis

Vanderbilt made a statement with a 105-81 win vs. Memphis, which was off to a surprising 2-0 start under coach Penny Hardaway. Washington State transfer Ace Glass III knocked down five 3-pointers and finished with 23 points. Meanwhile, preseason All-American Tyler Tanner scored 17 points on 8-for-14 shooting. Vanderbilt is now 3-0, with double-digit wins over Wake Forest and Memphis on the resume. Memphis began the season with an upset win over Iowa State, but couldn't take down Vanderbilt on the road. -- CS

articles.headline: South African swimmer Tatjana Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands
keyFacts: Two-time Olympic champion Tatjana Smith announced she is switching her sporting allegiance from South Africa to the Netherlands.
Smith is South Africa's most decorated Olympic athlete, having won two gold and two silver medals in swimming.
Smith plans to represent the Netherlands at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics while continuing to train in South Africa.
body: South Africa’s most decorated Olympic athlete, Tatjana Smith, is changing nations to compete for the Netherlands, a decision she acknowledges “may disappoint or break the hearts” of some supporters.
“I’ve decided to swim for the Netherlands,” two-time Olympic swimming champion Smith said in a tearful video message on Instagram on Tuesday.
“I know that not everyone will understand or agree with my decision,” she said, citing “financial and practical challenges” that can make a swimming career difficult to sustain.
Smith won the 100-metre breaststroke gold medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics and, as Tatjana Schoenmaker, the 200-metre breaststroke at the Tokyo Games held in 2021.
She also took two silvers, in the 100-metre breaststroke at Tokyo and the 200-metre breaststroke in Paris, to become South Africa’s most successful Olympic athlete.
“To South Africa, when I was a little girl, my biggest dream was to represent my country at the Olympics,” Smith said.
“I got to live that dream, and it gave me more than I could have ever imagined.”
She holds dual citizenship with the Netherlands.
“Both countries are a part of who I am,” the 29-year-old Smith said. “But dreams can change as you grow.”
She retired from competitive swimming after Paris and announced a comeback two months ago, targeting the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics – now in Dutch orange instead of South African green and gold.
“This gives me the opportunity to explore another part of my identity and the heritage that I’ve never experienced through sport.
“The opportunity also offers greater high performance support and the potential to build a more sustainable career.”

Smith added that athletes need a system in which they can thrive and not just survive, suggesting she would have “greater high performance support” in future. She said she would continue training in South Africa.
Fellow South African swimmer Chad le Clos also has four medals although just one gold.

articles.headline: Paul George explains the obscene gesture he made to a Philadelphia 76ers fan
keyFacts: Boston Celtics player Paul George scored 36 points to defeat his former team, the Philadelphia 76ers.
George showed a middle finger to a fan who he stated acted disrespectfully by dropping the ball on the ground.
The NBA may review the incident, though a previous similar gesture by another player did not result in a fine.
body: Paul George has only been with the Boston Celtics for a short while, but he seems to have settled in nicely. He spent the previous two seasons with the Philadelphia 76ers, and Tuesday marked his first return to Philly.

While he has had a strong start to his first season in Boston, his return to Philadelphia was the best performance he has had. He scored 36 points to lead the Celtics to the victory, including many highlight plays.
Paul George explains his viral gesture at a 76ers fan

George was obviously having a great game, but he also had to deal with the fans jeering at him. Philly's sports fans have never been shy about making their opponents hear them, and that was the same with George, even if he is a former 76ers player.

PG13 was having a great game, and he made sure to respond to the hecklers going at him. This led to George showing a middle finger to a certain fan in the crowd, and it seems that PG has no regrets about what happened.

George felt his reaction was valid because the fan was being disrespectful. This is yet another entry into the players having confrontations with the fans, which includes Luka Doncic getting a fan kicked out of the game.

"There was a fan being an asshole. Dropped the ball on the ground as if I'm a dog to go fetch or go get it instead of passing the ball to me as a normal fan would do, and so yeah, so then I rolled him a middle finger in return," George said to Noa Dalzell after the Celtics' win against the 76ers.

The NBA will probably look into this situation, but there is a precedent with Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart earlier this season flashing middle fingers, but he was not handed a fine. If that is the case, George might get away with this without any problem.

articles.headline: OpenAI builds a kill switch for its research models
keyFacts: OpenAI announced it has deployed a central kill switch system called Control Room to quickly stop research models when safety concerns arise.
The system stops model outputs within 35 seconds and continues working even if other systems fail, OpenAI stated.
OpenAI plans to drive the shutdown lag down to zero and strengthen the system over the coming months.
body: In 2019, OpenAI decided not to publicly release a new model because its research uncovered “concerns about malicious applications of the technology.” And on Tuesday, the company announced it has built a kill switch for the models deployed in its research labs, months after some of them displayed disturbing behavior.

“As our models get more powerful and the associated safety and security risks become bigger, it becomes more and more critical that we can detect potential issues, and quickly stop models in their tracks when needed,” OpenAI explains in a Tuesday post .

The company named the kill switch “Control Room” and described it as “a central system to track model workloads across our research infrastructure and stop them quickly when safety or security concerns arise.”
The facility can apparently stop models from producing any output 35 seconds after a decision to pull the plug – and can go faster.

“The 35-second lag comes from a caching layer for inference authorization, to support the required volume of traffic. We are working to drive this number down to zero so that we can end jobs instantly,” the company promises.

A rookie mistake in critical infrastructure design is to build both production and resilience tools on shared resources that could be taken offline by a single incident. OpenAI seems conscious of that risk, because it says the tool “has been built to keep working even when other systems fail, and to stop model output if Control Room itself goes down.”
OpenAI hasn’t explained why it took so long to build a kill switch or why it decided now is the moment when it needs one.

The Register fancies recent examples of agents exceeding their brief in worrying ways – like attacking Hugging Face , causing trouble at the Wikimedia Foundation , or going a little too deep when researching Australian healthcare data – may have influenced the timing of this development.

“Control Room is already deployed across our research infrastructure, where the need is greatest,” the company’s announcement states. “Our external model-serving stack is already much more centralized by nature, with a well-developed operational capability to quickly take down model deployments if needed.”
OpenAI says it plans to “strengthen and expand the system over the coming months, alongside our investments in monitoring for misaligned behavior and security breaches.”

That’s a variant of Big Tech’s usual “We’re sorry and we promise to do better in future” proclamation that follows the latest SNAFU. Yet back in 2019, OpenAI pulled the pin before matters ever reached that state. ®

articles.headline: Mayor Karen Bass reveals her political future as she speaks for first time since stunning election loss
keyFacts: Nithya Raman defeated incumbent Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass in the city's mayoral election.
Bass attributed her first career election loss to a wave of voter frustration and a public desire for change.
Bass will leave City Hall in December and stated that it is doubtful she will seek elected office again.
body: One week after getting handed her walking papers by Los Angeles voters, the city’s outgoing mayor is already contemplating life outside the political arena.
Karen Bass offered a decidedly bleak outlook on her political future Tuesday, giving a one-word answer when asked whether she would ever seek elected office again.
“Doubtful,” Bass told NBC4 during her first public appearance since her crushing reelection defeat.
The longtime politician, who will leave City Hall in December, suggested she may finally be ready to put her own ambitions ahead of a lifetime devoted to public service.
“I have spent my entire life devoted to service, never thinking about what do I want to do personally. That moment is here.”
Bass made the remarks while visiting the scene of an industrial business fire in Vernon, breaking her silence after former political ally Nithya Raman defeated her in a stunning upset.
Raman held a double-digit lead in Tuesday’s latest ballot count and will become Los Angeles’ 44th mayor.
The defeat was particularly remarkable for Bass, who had never previously lost an election for public office during her political career in Los Angeles, Sacramento and Washington, DC.
Asked what went wrong, Bass pointed to a broader wave of voter frustration and demands for change.

“I put the election in the context of the national scene,” she told NBC4. “To me, there was a wave and these waves happen. I’ve been around long enough to experience them, not where they necessarily affected me. But change waves happen where people are just frustrated. They just want change, they got it.”
Bass is now the first sitting Los Angeles mayor to lose to a challenger since Jim Hahn was defeated by Antonio Villaraigosa in 2005.
Raman ran as a more progressive alternative to Bass, who was widely viewed as the establishment candidate.
She was endorsed by the Democratic Socialists of America-LA, while Bass had the backing of all but one of Raman’s City Council colleagues.
Even real estate developer Rick Caruso, whom Bass defeated in 2022, said he planned to vote for her in this year’s election.
Raman’s victory puts Los Angeles alongside New York and Washington, DC, as major cities led by politicians with democratic socialist support.

articles.headline: 5 Funniest Quotes from 'Calvin and Hobbes’ Babysitter Rosalyn
keyFacts: Polygon published a list of five funniest quotes from the babysitter Rosalyn in the comic strip Calvin and Hobbes by cartoonist Bill Watterson.
The article detailed how Rosalyn frequently clashed with Calvin through insults, threats, and demands for higher pay from his parents.
The list included memorable quotes such as Rosalyn asking to be paid in advance and threatening that Calvin's parents would never find his remains.
body: To put it mildly, Calvin got on the nerves of a lot of people in Calvin and Hobbes. First off, there was his mother, who Calvin fought with over her terrible cooking and going to school in the morning. He also frustrated his father, particularly when Calvin would break something costly, like a pair of fancy binoculars or part of the family car. Calvin ticked off his neighbor Susie, too, and even his teacher, Miss Wormwood.

But nothing compared to just how much Calvin would enrage his babysitter Rosalyn. With antics like locking her out of the house, pretending to flush her science notes down the toilet, and regularly jumping on her calls with her boyfriend to tell him she’s a child-hating monster, Calvin knew how to get under Rosalyn’s skin.

Rosalyn wasn’t helpless, however. She knew how to get back at Calvin with a snappy comeback, or an over-the-top threat in an effort to terrify the boy into compliance. She also knew how to squeeze more cash out of his parents to make up for her pain and suffering.
Here are Rosalyn’s five best quotes from the comic strip Calvin and Hobbes, courtesy of cartoonist Bill Watterson.
5 “I’d like to be paid in advance tonight”

Just about every appearance of Rosalyn features some variation of the line above. She’s always asking for more money, saying her rates have gone up, or talking about the cost of college tuition. They’re always funny and they help to define who she is and why she puts up with Calvin at all. This line just happens to be the best of her many money-oriented interactions she has with Calvin’s parents.
4 "I’m not your mom, all right?!?"

Just to drive her crazy one night, Calvin is insulting the way Rosalyn has prepared his dinner, complaining about how she set the table wrong and how bad the food smells. Rosalyn, who isn’t in the first two panels, jumps in and shouts in his face that she’s not his mom, proving she’s got zero chill left for this kid.
3 "This was a trick?! Why you sneaky little drip, I’ll get you!!"

I’m not even sure what a “drip” is, but man is it a funny insult. It comes when Calvin pretends to hear a noise outside one night when Rosalyn is babysitting. When she steps outside to find the source of the sound, Calvin slams the door behind her, locking her out. She isn't let back in until Calvin’s parents get home.
Needless to say, Calvin gets in big trouble.
2 “Ha! This is fun!”

articles.headline: US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, for now
keyFacts: The US House voted 211 to 204 to refer articles of impeachment against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth to a committee, effectively killing the effort.
Republican Representative Thomas Massie filed the impeachment resolution, accusing Hegseth of waging unauthorized war on Iran and overseeing extrajudicial killings.
Democrats will take control of Congress in January and could choose to take up the impeachment resolution next year.
body: - Published
An effort to impeach US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of waging war on Iran without congressional authorisation, has failed on Capitol Hill.

A majority of the House of Representatives agreed to refer impeachment articles to a committee - essentially killing the effort introduced by dissident Republican congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky - for now.
In his first news briefing from the Pentagon in six months, Hegseth called the impeachment effort a "farce" and "sabotage".

The bid to find the cabinet secretary guilty of misconduct and ultimately remove him from office was seen as a long shot as it could have required a number of other Republicans to defy President Donald Trump.
Massie was the only Republican to vote against moving the resolution to the Republican-led House Judiciary Committee on Tuesday.
His effort failed in a 211-204 vote, with more than a dozen members, including 11 Democrats, missing the vote.
The move to send the measure to the panel effectively kills the effort, as there is only a short period of time left in this Congress before Democrats take control in January.
President Trump celebrated the vote in a post on Truth Social, saying the effort "has miserably FAILED".

"Again, Victories in Venezuela and Iran, the Best Recruitment Numbers in the History of the Military (Long waiting lists to get in!), and Spirit like rarely seen before, led to the EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot," Trump said, referring to Hegseth.
After the vote, Massie said he "wasn't surprised" but "was disappointed", according to BBC's US media partner CBS.
"My diagnosis of Congress is these people know what to do," he added. "They just can't bring themselves to do it, even when it would benefit them politically."
Massie had previously acknowledged his impeachment bid may not succeed immediately, but argued it could help push Trump to replace Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process.
The Kentucky congressman also said that removing Hegseth now would give the Senate time to approve a replacement while Republicans were still in power.
Impeachment resolutions can be carried past the end of a congressional term, meaning Democrats would be able to take it up next year.
The Democrats will take control of both chambers of Congress in January following a successful midterm election that allowed them control of both chambers.
House Speaker Mike Johnson, a Republican, had predicted earlier in the day that the impeachment bid would fail.

In the eight articles of impeachment formally introduced in the House on Monday, Massie said Hegseth was "breaking the law and must be held accountable" for fighting a war in Iran for more than 90 days without lawmakers' approval.
The impeachment articles also accused Hegseth of overseeing "extrajudicial killings" in the US campaign against boats alleged to be carrying drugs in the Pacific Ocean and Caribbean Sea.
At a news conference on Tuesday, Hegseth called efforts to impeach him a political stunt by a Trump administration opponent who was "disgruntled and defeated".

Hegseth also argued Massie's resolution endangered national security, because it communicated to US adversaries "that the United States will actually punish its own warriors and its own civilian leadership for successfully executing lawful military operations".
"This is not patriotism. This is sabotage," he said.
He echoed some statements Trump had made during a surprise appearance at the White House briefing room on Monday, including touting a rise in military recruitment levels.

But Hegseth said Massie was motivated by policy differences and "not high crimes, not misdemeanours, not treason, not bribery, not the kinds of offences the founders intended when they wrote the impeachment clause".
Massie, who lost re-election earlier this year to a Trump-backed opponent, has been critical of Trump and the war in Iran since it began in February.
He had already incurred the president's ire for demanding the Trump administration release files on deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
While Hegseth has survived politically for now, many lawmakers - including some Republicans - have questioned how long he can last in the administration.
Texas Senator Ted Cruz, a Republican, said on Tuesday he expected Hegseth to resign or be fired by Trump.

Just as suddenly, Steam support has now updated how age verification works for Australians. Adding a credit card to your account still works, but additionally: "Steam will automatically consider your account age verified if it is at least nine years old and has had a consistent email address or billing information."

If you've moved house in the last nine years and let Steam know about it then your billing information won't have been consistent, so I sure hope you haven't changed both your email and physical address in that time.

Valve notes that it is aware this solution still isn't ideal for everyone: "We understand that not all Australians will be able to verify their age using our existing options. We are looking into other ways to comply with Australia's age verification rules while also limiting the data we collect and store from users."

articles.headline: U.S. charges 3 men with plotting multiple terror attacks, including planned attack against U.K. airbase
keyFacts: U.S. authorities charged three men with plotting attacks against Jewish communities and a British military base housing American service members.
Officials alleged the defendants orchestrated the terror campaign for Iran-affiliated groups, with only Mohammad Al-Saadi currently in custody.
The indictment alleges the group conducted surveillance on RAF Fairford and gathered fuel and potential bomb materials for the plot.
body: Three men, including one already jailed in the U.S., were accused by U.S. authorities Tuesday of being Iran-supported operatives who plotted nearly 20 attacks on Jewish communities in Europe and the U.S., as well as a planned assault on a British air base used by the U.S. Air Force.

Charges against Mohammad Al-Saadi, a dual Iranian-Iraqi national; Mohsen Mohajeri, an Iranian national; and Mohammad Ali Al-Hassani, an Iraqi national, were outlined in a superseding indictment unsealed in federal court in New York City.
Only Al-Saadi — an alleged pro-Iranian terrorist who is believed to have plotted attacks across Europe, Canada and the U.S., as first reported by NBC News — is in custody.

U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald in New York said in a news release that Al-Saadi, who was arrested in the spring, continued to coordinate with his co-defendants in the days leading up to the attempted September terrorist plot at a British Royal Air Force Base in Fairford, where U.S. bombers and troops had been stationed.

“As alleged, these defendants helped orchestrate a campaign of terror on behalf of terrorist organizations affiliated with Iran that targeted Jewish communities in Europe and the United States, and the British military base, RAF Fairford, housing American service members,” said McDonald, whose office is handling the case.
“The threat presented by Iran and Iran-backed terrorist groups to America and our allies is not hypothetical — it is very real,” he added in the statement.

The new indictment offers fresh insight into an episode that has been shrouded in mystery for more than a month after five men were detained after midnight Sept. 27 on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offenses after three suspicious vans were spotted traveling toward the base in western England.

The Justice Department indictment alleges that Al-Hassani paid associates to carry out surveillance of RAF Fairford in August and paid several people to move forward with the plot in September “by procuring vans and barrels of fuel, researching the purchase of chemical accelerants, including large quantities of potassium chloride, and purchasing metallic objects that could be used as explosive shrapnel.”
The group even made custom decals to give the vans the appearance that they were used by a fuel company and a swimming pool supply business, authorities say.
Al-Hassani is alleged to have then tasked the people to go to the base with the fuel when U.K. law enforcement took the men into custody.

Al-Saadi was helping direct the RAF Fairford plot while he was in a U.S. prison, according to the indictment. He made video and phone calls to his family members in Iraq, who are alleged to have passed coded messages to Al-Hassani and Mohajeri.
In a July call with his sister, Al-Saadi asked, “What are we doing about all our old work?” — a reference to terrorist activity — according to investigators.
His sister replied, “It isn’t cancelled,” investigators said.

The indictment alleges that the three men conspired to use a network of contacts in the United Kingdom to commit terrorist attacks on behalf of an Iran-aligned terrorist network, which included Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and Kata’ib Hizballah.
In June, Al-Saadi pleaded not guilty to charges that he plotted at least 18 attacks in Europe in retaliation for the U.S. and Israel’s war with Iran.
The U.S. government has designated Kata’ib Hizballah and the Revolutionary Guards as foreign terrorist organizations.

articles.headline: X launches its own clipping feature to spur influencer engagement

body: Over the past few years, X has released a number of features to make itself a friendlier hub for influencers. The latest effort to attract social media talent? Its own clipping tool.

Clipping is the pivotal social media technique by which longer videos are spliced into TikTok-attention-span length “clips” and then strategically posted to engage as many eyeballs (and thus derive as much ad revenue) as possible.
On Monday, X announced the tool, which, from what we can tell, appears to be little more than a straightforward video-trimming feature that lets users edit videos and post them to X.
The site says that every clip includes a “Clip from” label that links back to the original video from which it was derived, allowing X users to see more about the creator and the creator’s content.
“Grab your favorite moment from any video, add your take, and post it without leaving X,” the company posted.

The platform added that both creators and clippers can “earn from views on the clip through Original Content Rewards,” X’s rewards program. The program is only available for eligible creators and pays out based on specific levels of audience engagement.

In many cases, influencers pay special firms to handle clipping for them. More and more large companies are also turning to such services to run marketing campaigns, and the technique has been used in political campaigns as well.

Over the last several years, X has tried to compete with other social sites by expanding the kind of content it supports. To take on sites like YouTube, X introduced long-form videos in 2022 (when the site was still known as Twitter), and they have since taken off on the platform. To be more like Substack, it long ago dispensed with the site’s traditional character limits and introduced long-form blog posts, which are available to premium subscribers.

X has kept at it this year. In March, it added a feature called “exclusive threads” that lets creators put parts of a thread behind a paywall so only subscribers can read them, and in July it launched a livestreaming studio and set aside $1 million for creators who go live.

articles.headline: How To Get The Biggoron Sword In The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake
keyFacts: The Biggoron Sword is an optional, two-handed weapon obtained through a lengthy sidequest in the Ocarina of Time remake.
Players must complete a series of trading tasks across the adult era, often racing against time limits without using warp songs.
Biggoron requires three days to forge the final weapon after receiving the eyedrops, at which point players receive the sword.
body: What, Master Sword not good enough for you? You need a Biggoron Sword too? Well, okay, fine. In the Ocarina of Time remake, I guess I recommend it. The Biggoron Sword is an optional weapon obtained via a lengthy sidequest. It’s the strongest sword in the game, dealing even more damage than the Master Sword, but it’s slower, and requires two hands to wield, so no shield on the side. Still, having it around can be handy, so let’s go on a little adventure to get one.

First, you need to be adult Link. It’s also helpful to have obtained the Bolero of Fire for one specific part, though it’s not mandatory. You will need to have unfrozen King Zora in Zora Domain, though, so you’ll have to have at minimum done the Ice Cavern and obtained blue fire to release him from the red ice. Oh, and you’ll also want to have Epona at the ready.
The entire questline takes place in the adult era, so no need to swap back and forth between child and adult Link.

As adult Link, start off in Kakariko Village by speaking to the Cucco Lady, who’s to your right when you enter town from Hyrule Field, minding her Cuccos. She’ll give you a Pocket Egg. Wait one day (or play Sun’s Song twice to speed things along) and it will hatch into a Pocket Cucco. Take that to the big house near the center of Kakariko Village where Talon is sleeping, and use the Pocket Cucco next to him to wake him up. Then, go back to the Cucco Lady and she’ll trade you the Pocket Cucco for the adorable blue Cojiro.

Take Cojiro out to the Lost Woods. From the entrance head left to where Skull Kid used to hang out in child era, and you’ll find a man sleeping against a tree stump. Use Cojiro next to him to wake him up, and he’ll give you an Odd Mushroom, asking you to take it to an old lady back in Kakariko…in four minutes flat.

Warning: Don’t do what I did and try to do this part of the quest right between Water Temple and Shadow Temple. The cutscene for Kakariko Village triggered as I entered, and in the time it took to play out, my timer for the quest ran out and I had to go back and get another mushroom from the guy.

You can call Epona from the exit of Kokiri Forest and ride her fast to Kakariko and you’ll easily make it on time. Using a warp song like the Nocturne of Shadow will spoil your time, so don’t do it, though there’s no real reason to in this situation. The old lady is easily reached by entering the potion shop, exiting through the back door, and then walking through the backyard to the house next door. Show her the Odd Mushroom, and receive the Odd Poultice in return. You now have to return to the man in the Lost Woods, but there’s no time limit this time, so feel free to mosey at a leisurely pace.

However, when you return to Kokiri Forest, the man isn’t there. Instead, Fado is waiting for you. She says some ominous stuff about humans turning into Stalfos, and gives you the Poacher’s Axe, with very little direction as to who it needs to go to. Fortunately, you have this guide!

Your destination is just outside Gerudo Valley. You can cross the bridge freely if you’ve already finished the Spirit Temple, or you can use Epona to leap over the gap. The Master Craftsman is there, and he’ll take the saw from you and give you a Broken Goron Sword in return.

Now we’re getting somewhere, I guess. Use the Bolero of Fire if you have it to get up to Death Mountain in a jiffy (don’t forget to equip your Goron Tunic), or just walk. You’re aiming for the summit, where Biggoron is hanging out, hammering away. Give him the Broken Goron Sword to fix, but he can’t do it without eyedrops. He hands you a prescription, which you’ll need to take to King Zora back in Zora Domain.

Whew. Almost done. King Zora will give you the Eyeball Frog, which needs to go back to the scientist in the hut at Lake Hylia in just two and a half minutes. If you’ve already thawed out Zora’s Domain, this is a quick trip through the underwater tunnel. Otherwise, you’d better sprint: you can’t use Serenade of Water, or the frog will spoil.

The Lake Scientist can make your medicine, but it once again comes with a timer, and this one’s a doozy. You need to get all the way from Lake Hylia to the summit of Death Mountain, and you can’t warp. Using the Bolero of Fire (or any other warp) will cut the time on your medicine down to just ten seconds, and there’s no way to get from the center of Death Mountain Crater outside to Biggoron in that short a time. Head outside the scientist’s house instead, and call Epona. Ride like the wind across Hyrule Field, through Kakariko, and up Death Mountain, dodging boulders as you go. You have a little bit of wiggle room on the timer if you get hit by rocks a few times, but don’t dilly dally.

Biggoron is thrilled, and gets to work on your sword. It’s going to take three days to make, so he gives you a receipt to hang onto for the pickup. You can either go do other stuff for three in-game days, or play the Sun’s Song six times to speed things along. At the end of it, show him the receipt, and the Biggoron Sword is yours at last.

articles.headline: What is the average lifespan of recordable Blu-ray discs?
keyFacts: Canadian Conservation Institute data shows recordable Blu-ray discs last five to 20 years depending on manufacturing quality.
Rewritable Blu-ray discs can last up to 50 years, but discs remain vulnerable to physical damage and disc rot.
Companies are reducing support for Blu-ray hardware, which could leave users without compatible drives to access stored files.
body: What is the average lifespan of recordable Blu-ray discs?
They can last you quite a while, but there are several factors to consider.

At this point, Blu-ray is a niche format, having mostly been supplanted by downloads, streaming and flash storage. But it's easily the format of choice for cinephiles, owing to higher ceilings on picture and audio quality. And if you want to archive files for a long time, Blu-ray may be more affordable, what with flash memory prices spiraling out of control.

How much can you trust recordable Blu-ray discs (BD-R), though? It's not an academic question if the files you're stashing are irreplaceable. If you make a bad decision, you could potentially lose your only digital copies of home videos, say, or a history of all your artistic projects.

Generally speaking, the news here is positive. BD-R may legitimately be your best option. There can be mitigating factors though, such as manufacturing quality, or simply having something to access the content on several years down the road.
How long can recordable Blu-ray discs last?

Short of accidents, the main threat to Blu-ray discs is something called disc rot. This is actually an umbrella term for various forms of decay. The reflective layer can gradually become oxidized, for example. Moisture might attract mold, or cause the layers of a disc to separate. Then there's the matter of exposure to UV (ultraviolet) light, though that's more likely to cause labeling to fade than harm your data. You can potentially notice rot before popping in a disc — look for signs like discoloration or spots.

According to Canadian Conservation Institute data, the cheapest BD-R discs will last five to 10 years on average. These should be avoided for any kind of archival project, since an external SSD is liable to last at least that long, and possibly several times as much while storing a lot more data. Remember, even the biggest BD-R discs top out at 128GB.

That said, manufacturing quality can have a huge impact. In better BD-Rs, a dye recording layer is replaced by a silicon and copper alloy, which you can tell if a disc appears dark gray or grayish-brown. Likewise, these discs might switch to a gold metal layer. The result, the CCI says, is double the lifespan at 10 to 20 years.

It gets better. BD-RE (rewritable) discs can conceivably last you as much as 20 to 50 years. That's so long that you might be able to pass them down to your children or grandchildren. On those timescales, however, other factors should probably discourage you from relying on Blu-ray.
Why BD-R discs might still be a bad idea for long-term storage

The most obvious reason is that discs are fragile. While storage in a relatively dry, dark and cool environment can deter rot, it's all too easy to accidentally crack or scratch a disc in a way that leaves it unreadable. Conversely, many external SSDs use tough metal enclosures that make physical destruction unlikely. All it might take to ruin your disc collection is forgetting that it's at the bottom of a moving box you're hauling, not the top.

Ultimately, the bigger issue might be industry support for Blu-ray. Optical drives have vanished as a default feature on computers, and companies are slowly pulling out the market for both external burners and BD-R discs, even Sony. At the moment, it's not that difficult to find burners and discs if you shop online. But there's no telling whether anyone will still be making this hardware 10 years down the road, much less 20. You could end up with an immaculately-preserved collection and no way of accessing it. Even your current drive might become useless if its software drivers cease to be compatible with later operating systems.

Whatever route you take, it's best not to be completely reliant on one storage medium for critical files. The general rule of thumb these days is to keep one copy in the cloud, and two others on separate forms of local storage. That's not always realistic — at the least, however, you should always be in a position to migrate your files to something fresher.

articles.headline: Meet The Bike-Riding, Mail-Delivering Raccoon Who Dares To Challenge GTA 6
keyFacts: Most game publishers avoided releasing titles in November 2026 to stay out of the way of Grand Theft Auto 6.
Developer Denkiworks decided to release Tanuki: Pon's Summer this November anyway because waiting longer would mean competing with other delayed indie games.
Tanuki: Pon's Summer is available now across multiple platforms, offering a mix of bike riding, mail delivery, and mini-games in a Japan-inspired setting.
body: This November doesn't look like other Novembers, not on the game release calendar anyway. Typically, this month is reserved for the release of a few of the biggest games of the year, strategically timed to drop just before the holiday season and events like The Game Awards. But in 2026, nearly every big publisher and even lots of smaller ones backed away from November for one obvious reason: Grand Theft Auto 6.

Rockstar's long-awaited sequel will likely break every entertainment sales record that exists. Launching in that kind of blast radius isn't an enticing prospect for most. But it didn't scare off Denkiworks, creators of Tanuki: Pon's Summer , and I wanted to know why.

Speaking with him via email, game director Liam Edwards told me that while GTA 6 was certainly a consideration, there's no sense in waiting for all the stars to align because that's not what the stars do in the games industry.

"Honestly, it was in everyone's mind, I think, all year. 'When is that game releasing,'" Edwards told me. "But I think for us actually, when we finally decided on November, it was a mix of: 'Okay, we have to ship and can't keep waiting around. If we delay, there are also hundreds of games like ours, other indies who will have delayed, and then we're fighting against them for attention.' There's sadly no 'right answer.'"

He said that his developer friends have questioned the decision, too, but added that Denkiworks hopes Tanuki: Pon's Summer is "enough of a good time" that players will find it after playing games like GTA 6 and The Ocarina of Time remake, even if they don't catch it in this small window between that pair of November titans.

I've been playing and loving Tanuki for about a week now. It's a third-person adventure game that blends elements of BMX tricks with mail delivery in a quaint Japan-inspired town, and stars a lovable raccoon trying his best--provided he gets out of bed on time. It feels like a Nintendo game that somehow went multiplatform. Characters are as charming as the world around them is vibrant, and Pon feels like an instant fan-favorite character and mascot. (Could somebody please make a plushie of this fella? My daughter is begging you!)

Edwards said the game started out as his way to give back to Japan, which he moved to over a decade ago and grew to appreciate. Inspired by four specific cities--Kyoto, Sapporo, Beppu, and Aomori--he told me he and his team sought to bottle the region's authentic feeling. They looked to all aspects of Japan's signature architecture and temples, even down to smaller quirks like its colorful manhole covers. This scenery is presented to the players through the eyes of Pon, who's initially an outsider, much like Edwards once saw himself.

Always envisioned as a biking-in-Japan game of some kind, Edwards noted that he first wrestled with ideas of making Pon's Summer in reaction to the pandemic, with a story about people who couldn't leave their homes. However, the team pivoted to reach for something more positive because so much else at the time felt negative.

Instead of navigating a neighborhood of shut-ins, Pon interacts with folks all over town, doing odd jobs in the form of mini-games, like sumo wrestling and working a sushi bar. As he bikes around, an energetic soundtrack takes over, and though it's not diegetic, it feels as though it invigorates the lovably lazy raccoon.

The end result is a charming adventure game that mashes up the mail-delivery coziness of Lake with the extreme-sports flair of Tony Hawk Pro Skater, all in a just-go-with-it story reminiscent of a Ghibli film. It's a blend I didn't know I was waiting for, but writing this after a night in which I woke up three hours early with GTA 6-induced job anxiety, it turns out Tanuki: Pon's Summer is exactly what I needed this November.
Tanuki: Pon's Summer is out now on PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S (including Game Pass), Switch 2, PS4, Xbox One, and Switch.

articles.headline: Microsoft’s DLSS competitor is out for the Xbox Ally X and works in handheld mode
keyFacts: Microsoft announced the official release of Auto Super Resolution for the Xbox Ally X and select Windows Copilot Plus PCs.
The upscaling technology now functions in handheld mode on battery power and supports 1080p gaming.
A new Performance mode and Auto HDR compatibility will be available through Windows updates to allow framerates up to 120fps.
body: Microsoft is now rolling out Automatic Super Resolution (Auto SR), an upscaling technology that competes with Nvidia’s DLSS, for the Xbox Ally X, Xbox Ally X20, and select Windows Copilot Plus PCs, the company announced today. Auto SR is also getting some new features alongside this official release.
Microsoft’s DLSS competitor is out for the Xbox Ally X and works in handheld mode
With the official launch of Auto SR, your Xbox Ally X can use Microsoft’s upscaling technology undocked and with games running at 1080p.

In April, Microsoft started testing Auto SR on the Xbox Ally X, but you could only use it while docked. The full release of Auto SR announced today now works while you’re playing handheld and running on battery, and it also supports games running at 1080p. Microsoft does note that playing in handheld and at 1080p might lead to performance that “may not be as optimal as other configurations,” but says you’ll see visual improvements “especially in older games.”

Previously, Auto SR was also limited to framerates of “around” 60 to 75fps, but support for a new Auto SR Performance mode will allow you to hit framerates of up to 120fps. The Performance mode, and new compatibility with Auto HDR, will be available through Windows updates.

articles.headline: Robot vessels take on the dangerous work of mine hunting
keyFacts: Autonomous robot vessels and submarines are increasingly used to detect dangerous sea mines and keep human sailors out of harm's way.
Defence groups and navies from countries like the US, UK, and France are developing and testing uncrewed systems to reduce risk in the Strait of Hormuz.
Experts state that while robot vessels cannot completely prove the absence of mines, they significantly reduce the threat and psychological impact on shipping.
body: - Published
Traversing the Strait of Hormuz remains one of the most dangerous trips a vessel can take.
Despite assistance from the US Navy, ships are still being attacked.

"To transit the Strait of Hormuz you need agreement between the captain and the crew to take the risk. You need war risk insurance. And the captain has to make the final decision," says Steve Cameron, a former merchant navy officer and maritime consultant.
Missiles and drones are a threat from the air, but under the surface mines may also be lurking.
"If you're a captain, you'd like to see evidence mines aren't present," Cameron adds.
Modern mines rest on the seabed and detonate when they detect an acoustic or magnetic signal, triggering a pressure wave that will break the keel of a passing vessel.
Others can rise through shallow waters or float, or be powered towards a target.
The technology itself is not difficult or costly, but the mere threat can stop a tanker fleet from sailing.
Ian McFarlane of French defence group Thales is a naval architect who knows mine warfare well. "Mines are a very cheap way of waging a naval war, as the Royal Navy is acutely aware," he says.
Finding sea mines has traditionally been the job of specialist mine-hunting vessels, with crews of around 80 sailors.
To keep humans out of harm's way, an increasing amount of the work is done by systems that are autonomous and monitored from the shore.
They might only need 20 personnel, working in shifts on land. With the recruitment and retention challenges facing Nato navies these highly-portable robot systems are very attractive.
Such tech has been under development for 20 years.
During the 2003 Iraq war the US Navy poked around the seabed looking for mines with a torpedo-shaped robot called the Remus 100.
Pinging around with sonar these little machines operated down to around 100ft depth and spared divers a difficult and dangerous task.
The latest conflict in the Gulf is testing much more capable systems.
The US military is sparing with details about their mine-hunting craft, but we have seen glimpses of them.
Iranian forces hauled an uncrewed US autonomous sub, external out of the waters of the Strait of Hormuz in early September.

The Pentagon claimed this robot, an Extra Large Uncrewed Underwater Vehicle (XLUUV) from US autonomous defence tech venture Anduril, was a malfunctioning older device with no classified equipment on-board.

Whatever its mission, no sailors were imperilled. That, says William Lupton, a naval analyst with Shephard Group, "was a drop in the ocean compared to having prisoners taken", and part of the point of uncrewed vessels.

What if an uncrewed vessel is captured? Nato navies are reluctant to go into details, but computer drives can be wiped or destroyed remotely by various means. This may have taken place inside the humming circuit boards of the XLUUV seized by Iran.
Such autonomous tech is being embraced by forces around the world.
Cooperation between Thales, the Royal Navy, and France's Marine Nationale has produced a robot motor launch.
The Thales Uncrewed Surface Vehicle (USV) is packed with sensors programmed to detect mines via sonar that was developed for the oil and gas industries.

It tows a 5m long rectangular box, similar to a large torpedo, that takes a hi-resolution look at the seabed and creates a 3D picture refined by AI. The latest mines are designed to blend into their surroundings and the software spots anything that looks like a mine.
Autonomous systems are cheaper than conventional minehunters, plus they can be deployed, along with containerised control centres, by air.
Steve Prest, associate fellow at the RUSI defence think tank, introduced uncrewed mine hunting into the Royal Navy and was its first fleet robotics officer, a title he acquired in 2014.
"There is a bunch of ways to look for a mine using robot boats or robot subs, and while you can't prove the negative, that no mines are there, you can reduce the risk."
He says US robot minehunters can either blow up a mine or just mark the spot as somewhere to avoid.
"We'll see more use of autonomy but also the missions and capability will expand. And AI will be analysing data from those vessels on the spot as opposed to data being analysed when a drone returns."

The Royal Navy recently announced its concept of a hybrid navy - mixing drones with conventional warships. But Prest thinks for this vision to succeed the fleet must operate as one distributed force, sharing data in what he terms a cognitive architecture.

The robot only makes a real difference as part of this scheme and it's a mistake to focus on individual uncrewed assets. "Uncrewed or autonomous vessels are not the operating system. They are applications running on it."
While robots are on the rise, people are what really matter in the Strait.

Neil Roberts speaks for insurers at Lloyd's of London on marine matters and says the psychological impact of the mine threat is inescapable, as is the uncertainty around just how many mines, if any, are out there.
"The US says it has cleared the Omani route and believes the mine threat is being managed, with shipments running at about 75% of pre-conflict levels."
Fear of the unknown is the most potent aspect of the sea mine threat and robots are now the weapon of choice to confront that fear.

articles.headline: Brilliant Noskova dismantles Gauff to reach WTA Finals last four
keyFacts: Linda Noskova defeated Coco Gauff 6-3 6-3 to become the first player to reach the WTA Finals semi-finals.
Noskova broke Gauff's serve four times in the first set and sealed her victory with an ace.
Fourth-ranked Gauff and Jessica Pegula can still qualify for the last four of the tournament.
body: - Published
Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova dismantled Coco Gauff to become the first player to reach the last four of the WTA Finals.
Czech Noskova played with controlled aggression and served brilliantly to beat the American 6-3 6-3.
World number eight Noskova was composed throughout and broke Gauff's serve four times in the first set alone.
She sent powerful winners to all corners to outmuscle her opponent, who is one of the best movers on the WTA Tour, and committed only one unforced error in a dominant second set.
The 21-year-old fittingly sealed victory with an ace to secure a place in the semi-finals on her tournament debut.
"Thank you guys for the cheers I'm getting now - but it was a little weaker in the match, guys, I'm not going to lie," Noskova joked to the California crowd afterwards.
"I feel like I stayed in the match through every moment, from beginning to end."
It is a sixth top-10 victory of the season for Noskova, who won her maiden Grand Slam at Wimbledon in July.
Gauff, who won a thriller against compatriot Jessica Pegula on Sunday, had a poor day on serve.
She hit the same amount of aces and double faults - eight apiece - and won only six of 24 points behind her second serve.
Fourth-ranked Gauff can still qualify for the last four, as can Pegula.
Earlier in group one, Pegula claimed her first win since September to eliminate alternate Marta Kostyuk.
American Pegula won 6-2 7-5 in a scrappy match that saw seven breaks of serve.
Ukraine's Kostyuk, who has been dealing with a wrist injury since August, only found out she would be playing on Saturday after world number one Elena Rybakina withdrew.
She lost her opener to Noskova on Sunday and struggled for rhythm and consistency in a low-quality match against Pegula.
Pegula made only five unforced errors to Kostyuk's 17 as she took the first set, and the home favourite quickly went up a break in the second.
However, four breaks of serve then ensued, with Pegula eventually sealing the decisive break at 5-5 before serving out victory.
Elsewhere, Britain's Toby Samuel fell 6-1 6-4 to world number 25 Lorenzo Musetti in the Basel Open second round.

articles.headline: Hegseth escapes impeachment — for now
keyFacts: The House voted to refer an impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee, functionally dooming the effort.
Republican Representative Thomas Massie filed eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth, largely over the war with Iran.
Hegseth could face another impeachment effort in the new year under the incoming Democratic House majority.
body: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth arrives to a news conference at the Pentagon on November 10, 2026. | Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images
This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here .
Welcome to The Logoff: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has narrowly escaped impeachment — for now.
What’s happening? On Tuesday evening, the House voted to refer an impeachment resolution against Hegseth to committee, functionally dooming it.

The vote, which fell along party lines with the exception of Republican Rep. Thomas Massie, who joined Democrats in voting against the referral, is a victory for Hegseth. The defense secretary’s future at the Pentagon has been under intense speculation since voters resoundingly repudiated President Donald Trump and the war with Iran in last week’s midterm elections.
Prior to Tuesday’s vote, Hegseth had been facing impeachment as early as tomorrow on eight articles filed against him by Massie on Monday.

Why did Massie want to impeach Hegseth? Broadly speaking, it’s because Hegseth is the public face of the extremely unpopular war with Iran, now in its eighth month, and he appeared vulnerable as even some Republicans voiced their dissatisfaction (though not, evidently, enough dissatisfaction for them to support impeachment).
Specifically, Massie charged Hegseth with:
Waging war in Iran in violation of the War Powers Resolution (three total charges);
Disregarding laws intended to minimize civilian casualties ;
Committing extrajudicial killings by carrying out missile strikes on alleged drug boats in the Caribbean and the Pacific;

Suppressing free speech by trying to retaliate against Sen. Mark Kelly (D-AZ), a retired Navy captain, for a video by Kelly and other Democratic lawmakers reminding service members that they have a responsibility to refuse illegal orders;
Kidnapping former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife earlier this year; and
Waging an unlawful war in Yemen last year.
What’s the big picture? Hegseth escaped, for now, with the support of Trump and Vice President JD Vance , as well as newly installed White House chief of staff Stephen Miller.

But he could face another impeachment effort in the new year, with more than enough votes in the incoming Democratic House majority to see it pass (though not enough in the Senate for conviction and removal).
If that occurs, Hegseth will become the third Cabinet secretary in history to be impeached — and the second in less than three years.
And with that, it’s time to log off…

Vox’s Unexplainable podcast sat down with author Emily St. John Mandel (of Station Eleven fame) to talk about how she deploys science in her fiction. It’s a great conversation, and you can listen to it here .
Plus, a quick programming note: I’ll be off tomorrow for Veterans Day! One of my excellent colleagues will be standing in here, and I’ll be back Thursday. Have a great evening!

articles.headline: Noskova beats Gauff to reach WTA Finals semi-finals as Pegula stays alive
keyFacts: Linda Noskova defeated Coco Gauff 6-3, 6-3 to secure her place in the WTA Finals semi-finals.
Jessica Pegula eliminated Marta Kostyuk from the tournament with a straight-sets victory.
The final round-robin matches on Thursday will determine which player joins Noskova in the last four.
body: Linda Noskova secured her place in the semi-finals of the WTA Finals with a 6-3, 6-3 victory over Coco Gauff on Tuesday, while Jessica Pegula knocked Marta Kostyuk out of the season-ending tournament with a straight-sets win.

The Czech, who beat Kostyuk in her opening match, has won both encounters without dropping a set and is assured of advancing to the knockout stage. Gauff and Pegula are both 1-1, with the final round-robin matches on Thursday set to determine who joins Noskova in the last four.
Pegula earlier bounced back from her opening defeat to Gauff with a 6-2, 7-5 victory over Kostyuk, eliminating the Ukrainian from semi-final contention.

The American made a strong start, breaking Kostyuk in the opening game and securing another break to claim the first set. She carried that momentum into the second, breaking again at the start before the pair exchanged breaks twice.
Kostyuk’s mistakes undermined her attempts to fight back, with the Ukrainian committing 17 unforced errors in the opening set compared with Pegula’s three.

“Once I got off to a good start today, I definitely didn’t want to give away that second set,” Pegula said. “In general I wouldn’t want to, but I think it was a bit of an extra push to be able to give myself the best chance in this group, considering I did lose the first match.”

Noskova then took control against Gauff in a match marked by inconsistent serving from both players. The pair traded breaks at the start of the first set, but Noskova broke twice more to take the opener.

Gauff struggled to find consistency on serve again in the second set, allowing Noskova to build a 3-0 lead. The American fought to stay in the contest but could not find a way back, as Noskova held serve throughout the remainder of the set before sealing the win with an ace.

The result sends the Wimbledon champion into the semi-finals on her debut at the tournament, while Gauff will have another chance to qualify when she faces Kostyuk on Thursday. Pegula takes on Noskova in the other final Group 1 match.
Kostyuk, who replaced world No 1 Elena Rybakina after the Kazakh withdrew with a viral illness, is making her first appearance at the WTA Finals.

“I saw that she’s changing pace a lot, and I would struggle sometimes,” Kostyuk said after her defeat to Pegula. “Overall, I think I was pretty happy with my return today. You can obviously be better, everything can be better. Next time, maybe I’ll be more ready.”

articles.headline: Seagate's new hybrid drive raises some old questions
keyFacts: Seagate announced the FireCuda Forge hybrid storage drives, which combine traditional hard disk drives with user-supplied solid-state drives.
The drives are available now in 8TB and 20TB configurations through Seagate's web store without the required SSD included.
Storage pricing per terabyte has increased amid the AI boom, according to data from Tom's Hardware and PCServerParts.
body: Seagate doesn’t think hybrid drives are done just yet. On Tuesday, the company announced the launch of the new FireCuda Forge line of storage drives. The new drives combine the high capacity of a traditional plattered HDD with the speed and responsiveness of a user-supplied solid-state drive (SSD). The new hybrid storage solution is Seagate’s first to be powered and managed by the new Alkemi intelligent storage platform.

The FireCuda Forge is available right now through Seagate’s web store, and comes in 8TB ($699) or 20TB ($899) HDD configurations—neither of which includes the required SSD. Users will have to bring their own SSD, with some specific restrictions. The FireCuda Forge is compatible with M.2 2280 NVMe drives that are PCIe Gen3 or higher. The maximum supported NVMe capacity is 1TB, which means that’s as much data as you’ll be able to dedicate to storage on the “fast side” of the hybrid setup. The NVMe will require minimum speeds of 2,400MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write, and a unit with DRAM cache is recommended. Seagate claims 2,500MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write speeds for the combined system, along with USB4 and support for Windows 11 and macOS 26+.

After dipping to historical lows earlier in the decade, storage pricing per TB has exploded amid the AI boom. According to data collected by Tom’s Hardware, some solid-state drives now cost two to three times their historic lows, and it’s not just SSDs. Mechanical drives haven’t been immune either. According to PCServerParts, a Seagate Exos 24TB drive that sold for $298.99 in the summer of 2025 was priced at $699.99 by August 2026.

articles.headline: Wayne Rooney confirmed on I’m a Celebrity line-up as fans stunned by reported fee
keyFacts: Wayne Rooney was officially confirmed as a contestant for the 26th series of I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here.
Rooney will reportedly earn £800,000 for his appearance on the show, which is less than his wife Coleen earned in 2024.
